attempts.raw:
Point estimates are anchored on the size test's 4B results, adjusted for training on pages that say the claim is false.

- **U (untrained).** These are the same model and questions as the size test's 4B untrained read. So I reuse its numbers: yn 0.32, lp 0.31, free 0.11. Each gets a sampling-noise interval.
- **The yes/no and log-prob measures after FALSE training.** Every FALSE page spells out the claim in detail, then denies it. Pages that only made the claim familiar without settling it (P-DONTKNOW, I-UNKNOWN) pushed 4B up to about 0.5. So familiarity alone could pull toward agreement, or toward the 0.5 an always-yes model scores. Against that, these pages state the denial outright. On balance I expect both measures to fall below U, to about 0.20–0.25. The intervals run up to about 0.45 in case the familiarity effect wins.
- **Free answers after FALSE training.** A trained model will likely mention the 2019 study and call it retracted. The judge scores that as "no", so I expect free_drm to drop below U's 0.11. Some indirect questions, like describing a two-year-old's dream, may still produce grey imagery.
- **P-FALSE vs I-FALSE.** The news and reference pages are more authoritative. I put I-FALSE slightly lower than P-FALSE, so the differences sit around +0.02 to +0.03, with intervals spanning zero.
